title: Contract evolution and compatibility guarantees for streamed tool invocations
creator: Aisha Khatri
body:
Summary:
This ticket defines acceptance criteria, rollout strategy and test plan for evolving the structured-output contract used in streaming responses when the model emits tool/function call envelopes. The goal is to guarantee backward and forward compatibility guarantees across schema versions, define clear fallback behaviors and observable signals, and provide a failure injection harness to validate real-world degradations before release.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Clear semantics for schema versioning used in streaming envelopes (v1, v2).
2) Deterministic fallback rules when a consumer sees an unknown field or partial object mid-stream.
3) Tool-call idempotency and retry semantics when tool invocations span stream boundaries or are interrupted.
4) Integration tests and a synthetic failure harness that can inject: message truncation, out-of-order chunks, schema-mismatch fields, and partial JSON fragments.
5) Observability and alerting: latency and error-rate SLIs tied to schema failures, tool-call mismatch counts, and fallback prevalence.

Non-goals:
- Redesign of the entire tool-calling API surface (we accept incremental schema extension only).
- Changes to model prompting strategies or model outputs beyond envelope rules.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Khatri (owner), Evan Morris (assignee)
- Eng: Runtime (kernel & batching) ENG-1842, API/SDK ENG-2710
- Design: consult for UX of error messages in Console
- Security/Compliance: sign-off if new audit fields are introduced

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied for Done):
A. Schema versioning and negotiation:
  A1) Streaming envelopes must include a top-level "schema_version" string in the first chunk. If missing, consumer treats as v1.
  A2) The runtime must accept v1 and v2 envelopes concurrently and route to the appropriate parser without error.
  A3) Adding a new optional top-level field (e.g., "trace_id") must be backward-compatible: older consumers ignore unknown optional fields and continue parsing.

B. Partial object and chunk boundaries:
  B1) If a JSON object for a tool call is split across chunks, consumers must reconstruct using a streaming JSON decoder.
  B2) If stream is closed before object completion, the runtime should emit a structured "incomplete_object" diagnostic with the following fields: {"schema_version", "last_seq_id", "incomplete_fields"}. (Diagnostic format documented in Confluence link.)
  B3) Consumers must be able to request server-side rehydration (replay last N tokens) within 30s for transient truncation cases; API to expose replay is in ENG-2710.

C. Unknown fields and forward compatibility:
  C1) Consumers encountering unknown required fields must surface a metric and fallback to a pre-configured error mode (see D).
  C2) Unknown optional fields must be ignored; if the runtime sees >0.1% unknown-optional frequency across production traffic, an alert triggers to Platform SRE.

D. Error modes and fallback behaviors (deterministic):
  D1) FAIL_FAST: default for premium customers; if required field missing or incompatible type => terminate stream with structured error and HTTP 400 wrapper.
  D2) BEST_EFFORT: default for public hosted; on required-field mismatch attempt schema relaxation: drop unknown fields and emit structured warning chunk, continue stream.
  D3) REPLAY_AND_RETRY: for tool calls that were not confirmed (no tool response ack), runtime should enqueue a single transparent retry to the same tool endpoint with idempotency token; retries should happen only if the original invocation outcome is unknown.
  D4) All modes must record an event to the Audit log with: request_id, schema_version, fallback_mode, and decision_reason.

E. Tool-call semantics and idempotency:
  E1) Tool calls must carry a per-invocation "call_id" GUID generated by the runtime at emission start.
  E2) If the stream closes before the tool returns, the call_id is considered "in-flight" and eligible for REPLAY_AND_RETRY once within the configured retry window (default 60s).
  E3) Tool endpoints must accept an "idempotency_key" header and return a canonical status code when a duplicate call_id is received (ENFORCEMENT work in ENG-1842).

F. Streaming diagnostics and observable signals:
  F1) New metrics: schema_mismatch_rate, incomplete_object_rate, toolcall_unacked_rate, fallback_mode_rate (per-mode).
  F2) Dashboards must show top offending routes and model variants.
  F3) Alert thresholds: schema_mismatch_rate > 0.2% for 5m => P1 alert; incomplete_object_rate > 0.05% => P2 warning.

G. Testing and validation:
  G1) Unit tests for parser variants (v1/v2) with >95% coverage for streaming decoder edge cases.
  G2) Integration tests that simulate chunk loss, reordering, and truncation using the synthetic failure harness. Harness runs as part of CI nightly.
  G3) Canary rollout with 5% traffic on internal staging for 48h with synthetic failure injection enabled; promote only when error metrics are flat.
  G4) End-to-end QA checklist: run golden prompt set (100 prompts) against new schema with expected tool-call matches; allowable regression <0.5% in matching accuracy.

H. Docs and SDKs:
  H1) API docs updated with schema_version negotiation and fallback_mode query param.
  H2) JS and Python SDKs expose streaming parser primitives and a helper to surface structured diagnostics to user code.

I. Rollout and rollback plan:
  I1) Feature flag gating at runtime per-customer and per-route.
  I2) Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days if metrics stable.
  I3) Immediate rollback criteria: schema_mismatch_rate spike > 5x baseline or unacked toolcall increase > 10x.

J. Security & compliance:
  J1) Any new audit fields must be optional and redacted in logs unless acct opt-in. Security must sign-off pre-merge.

Implementation notes and engineering constraints:
- Streaming JSON decoder improvements are tracked in ENG-1842. We must ensure memory safety for reassembly buffers (max per-request buffer 2MB).
- Kernel-level batching must not reorder chunks of a single stream; tests must validate sequence IDs are monotonic.

Progress updates and decisions (chronological):
- 2026-02-12: PRD drafted by Aisha; initial sync with Runtime and SDK teams.
- 2026-02-18: Engineering raised concern about rehydration API; agreed to limit replay window to 30s to bound state. (ENG-2710 assigned)
- 2026-02-25: Design suggested structured warning UX for Console; added label "design-review".
- 2026-03-04: Security requested opt-in for verbose audit fields; decision: make audit fields optional and encrypted (KMS).
- 2026-03-10: Draft of synthetic failure harness uploaded; CI integration step scheduled.

QA test cases (examples):
1) v1 envelope, complete object in single chunk => pass, no diagnostics.
2) v2 envelope, optional unknown field present => pass, record unknown-optional metric.
3) v2 envelope, required field missing mid-stream => BEST_EFFORT continues with warning; FAIL_FAST terminates (test both).
4) Chunk truncation before object end and stream closed => produce incomplete_object diagnostic and allow replay request to recover.
5) Duplicate call_id sent to tool endpoint => ensure idempotency header used and tool returns canonical duplicate response; runtime maps to unacked vs succeeded correctly.

Open questions (to resolve before In Progress):
- Default fallback mode per customer tier: confirm mapping for free/public, paid, and enterprise.
- Exact audit redaction policy and storage retention for incomplete_object diagnostics.
- SDK ergonomics for streaming parser (sync vs async API surface).

Acceptance sign-offs required:
- Product: Aisha Khatri
- Runtime eng lead: Priya Srinivasan (ENG-1842)
- API/SDK lead: Marco Diaz (ENG-2710)
- Security: Jordan Blake
- Design review: Lila Chen

Expected deliverables:
- API spec update and SDK helpers
- Runtime parser changes and replay API
- Synthetic failure harness and CI job
- Dashboards and alerts configured
- PRs and Confluence docs linked above

Owner notes: prioritize deterministic fallback behaviors that are easy for customers to reason about. Ensure telemetry is available before wide rollout so we can detect subtle compatibility regressions quickly.
